docs.title: Install NixOS on a VPS
docs.text:
This step is crucial for the installation process. The partitioning varies depending on whether you’re using MBR or GPT. In this guide, we will use MBR. However, if there’s demand for a GPT example, I may update the tutorial in the future.

# Replace /dev/sdX with your actual device you want to partition.

# 1. Create a MBR partition table.
parted /dev/sdX -- mklabel msdos

# 2. Add the root partition. This will fill the the disk except for the end
#    part, which we will need for the swap and installer.
parted /dev/sdX -- mkpart primary 1MB -18GB

# 3. Set the root partition’s boot flag to on. This allows the disk to be 
#    booted from.
parted /dev/sdX -- set 1 boot on

# 4. Add the installer partition
parted /dev/sdX -- mkpart primary -18GB -8GB

# 5. Add a swap partition. The size required will vary according
#    to needs, here a 8GB one is created.
parted /dev/sdX -- mkpart primary linux-swap -8GB 100%

I assume you are booted into Arch Linux and have SSHed into it. There are many different ways to install Nix. I used the Determinate Nix Installer.

# 1. Mount the installation partition
mkdir /nix
mount /dev/disk/by-label/installer /nix
mkdir /nix/xdg_cache_home
export XDG_CACHE_HOME=/nix/xdg_cache_home

# 2. Install Nix
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf -L https://install.determinate.systems/nix | sh -s -- install

# 3. Get started using Nix:
. /nix/var/nix/profiles/default/etc/profile.d/nix-daemon.sh

# 4. install NixOS's installation tools
nix-env -f '<nixpkgs>' -iA nixos-install-tools

# 1. Mount the target file system on which NixOS should be installed on /mnt,
#    e.g.
mount /dev/disk/by-label/nixos /mnt

# 2. The command nixos-generate-config can generate an initial configuration 
#    file for you.
nixos-generate-config --root /mnt

# 3. You should then edit /mnt/etc/nixos/configuration.nix to suit your needs.
nano /mnt/etc/nixos/configuration.nix

docs.title: Install NixOS on a VPS¶
docs.text: If your VPS provider doesn’t offer a direct NixOS image, you can still install NixOS from a Rescue Environment. Let’s explore how.

docs.title: Format parttitions¶
docs.text:
# 1. Format the root partition
mkfs.ext4 -L nixos /dev/sdX1

# 2. Format the installer partition
mkfs.ext4 -L installer /dev/sdX2

# 3. Format the swap partition
mkswap -L swap /dev/sdX3

docs.title: Example of hardware-configuration.nix.¶
docs.text:
{ config, lib, pkgs, modulesPath, ... }: {
  imports = [ (modulesPath + "/profiles/qemu-guest.nix") ];
  boot.initrd.availableKernelModules =
    [ "ata_piix" "uhci_hcd" "virtio_pci" "virtio_scsi" "sd_mod" ];
  fileSystems."/" = {
    device = "/dev/disk/by-uuid/a4ec759d-deff-4986-8fee-b6aea1b80c9c";
    fsType = "ext4";
  };
  swapDevices =
    [{ device = "/dev/disk/by-uuid/96da0bfe-4037-4309-8ece-9e8df98b4dcb"; }];
  networking.useDHCP = lib.mkDefault true;
  nixpkgs.hostPlatform = lib.mkDefault "x86_64-linux";
}

docs.title: Example for configuration.nix¶
docs.text:
{ config, lib, pkgs, ... }:
{
  imports = [ ./hardware-configuration.nix ];
  
  boot.loader.grub.enable = true;
  boot.loader.grub.device = "/dev/sda";
  boot.initrd.checkJournalingFS = false;

  time.timeZone = "Europe/Tirane";
  i18n.defaultLocale = "en_US.UTF-8";

  # Define a user account. Don't forget to set a password with 'passwd'.
  users.users.alice = {
    isNormalUser = true;
    extraGroups = [ "wheel" ];
    packages = with pkgs; [ tree ];
    openssh.authorizedKeys.keys = [
      "ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3N..."
    ];
  };
 
  services.openssh = {
    enable = true;
    passwordAuthentication = true;
    permitRootLogin = "yes";
  };

  system.stateVersion = "24.11";
}

docs.title: Example of flake.nix¶
docs.text:
{
  description = "Alice's NixOS configuration";
  inputs = {
    nixpkgs.url = "https://flakehub.com/f/NixOS/nixpkgs/0.2405.635688.tar.gz";
  };
  outputs = { self, nixpkgs, nixos-hardware, ... }@inputs: {
    nixosConfigurations.nixos = nixpkgs.lib.nixosSystem {
      system = "x86_64-linux";
      modules = [
        ./configuration.nix
      ];
    };
  };
}

When you are happy with your configuration, run:

nixos-install --root /mnt

# When prompted enter the new root password

Now you can reboot and enjoy your NixOS VPS!

model.fit(X, Y)
theta0 = model.intercept_[0]
